title.title: Exact Fourier transforms below $n \log n$
title.subtitle: Claim: the length-$n$ DFT in $O\big(n(\log n)^{1-10^{-13}}\big)$ operations, in exact complex arithmetic

beats.text: The FFT: $\log_2 n$ stages of $n/2$ butterflies, $O(n \log n)$ operations
Zoom in on the exponent of $\log n$ by a factor of $10^{13}$

before.label: Best known since 1965
before.note: an $\Omega(n \log n)$ lower bound was proved only in restricted models

achievement.note: Refutes $\Omega(n \log n)$ for unrestricted linear circuits, by a hair

verify.detail: In Lean: for every $c > 0$, some $n$ has a circuit below $c\,n \log_2 n$. Not the $10^{-13}$ algorithm
verify.ourCheck: We recomputed the paper's constants; we did not build the Lean

sources.quote: O(n (log n)^{1-10^{-13}}) operations in an exact complex-arithmetic model with unrestricted coefficients
Morgenstern (1973) Omega(n log n) for bounded-coefficient linear circuits
refuting an Omega(n log n) lower bound for unrestricted complex linear circuits
ExactFourier.lean covers only the subsequential nonuniform circuit result (for every c>0 some n has a circuit with < c n log2 n gates); the every-length uniform algorithm is not formalized

sources.ref: article, FFTW and cuFFT are unaffected

sources.quote: I recomputed every constant in (1.1) and (2.4)–(2.10) with exact integers
I did not build it or run Comparator
'An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform' (31 pp)

plain: The FFT splits a signal into its frequencies; since 1965 nobody had shown it could take fewer steps

steps: One small 2-by-2 step can be done a little cheaper
Nest it inside copies of itself, again and again
The tiny saving compounds across the whole transform

data.label: a saving that grows with every level

voice.text: Since nineteen sixty five, n log n. Zoom in: the saving is tiny.
One slightly cheaper step, nested inside itself, compounds into a saving.
It beats n log n, by a hair.
